intervals.label: air-Cherenkov experiments in the valley
intervals.note: "Active" is open-ended because the TAIGA collaboration's 2022 overview describes the facility as in operation; no later source was read.
intervals.quote: The experiments to detect EASs by their Cherenkov radiation in the Tunka valley 50 km to the west from Lake Baikal (51.49 N, 103.04 E) were begun in 1993.

name: Tunka Valley (TAIGA astrophysical facility)
notes: No operator is recorded: the TAIGA lecture names Leonid Kuzmichev as the head of the Tunka facility but no operating institution.
The TAIGA website (taiga-experiment.info) returned HTTP 404 and the other candidate hosts did not resolve (checked 2026-10-26).

altitude.quote: The Tunka-133 array is located at an altitude of 670 m a.s.l.

summary.plain: The Siberian valley near Lake Baikal where the Tunka-133 cosmic-ray array, the Tunka radio array and the hybrid TAIGA gamma-ray detectors operate.
summary.technical: Tunka astrophysical facility, 50 km west of the southern tip of Lake Baikal; since 1993 it grew from Tunka-4 (four phototubes) through Tunka-25 and Tunka-133 to the TAIGA complex (2012 onward).
